question: A company runs a database server on EC2 around the clock with a stable, predictable load for the next three years. It will not change instance families. Which purchasing option gives the lowest cost?
explanation: A 3-year Standard Reserved Instance gives the deepest RI discount (up to 72%) for steady, predictable usage. Convertible RIs and shorter terms discount less, and Spot Instances can be interrupted, which a database cannot tolerate.

question: A company wants a Reserved Instance discount but expects to switch instance families and operating systems during the term. Which option should it purchase?
explanation: Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged for RIs with a different instance family, operating system or tenancy. Standard RIs offer a larger discount but cannot be exchanged for a different instance family.

question: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate and wants one flexible commitment that discounts all three. Which pricing model fits?
explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 in any family or Region, Lambda and Fargate in exchange for a 1- or 3-year hourly spend commitment. EC2 Instance Savings Plans give a bigger discount but cover only one instance family in one Region and do not cover Lambda or Fargate.

question: A research team runs image-rendering batch jobs that can stop and restart at any time without harm. Which EC2 purchasing option minimizes cost?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off On-Demand prices but can be reclaimed with a two-minute warning, which interruption-tolerant batch jobs can absorb. Reserved Instances need a 1- or 3-year commitment that a flexible batch workload does not justify.

question: A company must bring existing server-bound software licenses priced per physical core and socket to AWS. Which EC2 option provides that visibility?
explanation: Dedicated Hosts give a whole physical server with visibility into sockets and cores, which bring-your-own-license terms often require. Dedicated Instances also run on single-tenant hardware but give no control over or visibility into the underlying host.

question: A retailer needs guaranteed EC2 capacity in one Availability Zone for a two-week sales event and wants no long-term commitment. Which option should it use?
explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration and can be cancelled at any time. Savings Plans lower the price but do not reserve capacity, and they require a 1- or 3-year commitment.

question: A developer wants to know which AWS Free Tier offers continue to apply no matter how old the AWS account is. Which offer type is this?
explanation: Always Free offers, such as 1 million AWS Lambda requests per month, do not expire. Twelve-month offers end a year after sign-up and short-term trials end after a set period from first use.

question: A company is estimating the network charges for a new web application. Which type of data transfer is generally free of charge?
optionA: Data transferred into AWS from the internet
optionB: Data transferred out of AWS to the internet
optionC: Data transferred between two AWS Regions
explanation: Inbound data transfer from the internet is generally not charged. Outbound transfer to the internet, cross-Region transfer and most cross-AZ transfer are billed per GB.

question: A law firm must keep scanned case files for ten years. The files are almost never read, and retrieval within 12 hours is acceptable. Which S3 storage class costs least?
explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive has the lowest storage price, with standard retrievals completed within 12 hours. Glacier Instant Retrieval returns data in milliseconds but stores it at a higher per-GB price than needed here.

question: An analytics team stores data with unpredictable, changing access patterns and wants storage costs optimized automatically without paying retrieval fees. Which S3 storage class should it choose?
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers based on use for a small monitoring fee and charges no retrieval fees. Standard-IA and One Zone-IA charge a per-GB retrieval fee, which adds up when access is unpredictable.

question: An AWS Partner that resells AWS wants to group customer accounts, apply its own pricing rates and produce pro forma bills for each group. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Billing Conductor lets you group accounts, define custom pricing rules and generate pro forma billing data for showback or chargeback. Cost Explorer only analyzes the actual AWS charges and cannot apply custom rates.

question: A team wants an email alert when its forecasted monthly AWS spending is expected to exceed $5,000. Which service meets this requirement?
explanation: AWS Budgets sends alerts when actual or forecasted cost or usage exceeds a threshold you set. Cost Explorer can show forecasts but does not send alerts, and a CloudWatch billing alarm watches only actual estimated charges.

question: A finance analyst wants to view charts of the last 12 months of spending by service and see a forecast for the coming months. Which tool should the analyst use?
explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interactive view of historical costs, filtering by service, account or tag, and cost forecasts. The Cost and Usage Report is the most detailed data, but it is delivered as raw files rather than ready-made charts.

question: Which AWS billing resource delivers the most granular, line-item cost and usage data to an Amazon S3 bucket for querying with Amazon Athena?
explanation: The AWS Cost and Usage Report writes the most comprehensive line-item billing data to S3, where Athena, Redshift or QuickSight can analyze it. CloudTrail records API activity, not costs.

question: A company planning a migration wants to estimate the monthly cost of a proposed architecture before creating any AWS resources. Which tool should it use?
explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator models the cost of services you have not deployed yet. Cost Explorer analyzes spending that has already happened, and Compute Optimizer right-sizes resources that are already running.

question: A company with 15 AWS accounts wants one monthly bill and wants usage combined across accounts to reach lower volume pricing tiers. Which feature should it use?
explanation: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations gives one bill for all member accounts, aggregates usage for volume discounts and shares Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts. IAM Identity Center centralizes sign-in, not billing.

question: A company wants its billing reports to break down AWS costs by department and project. What should the company do?
optionB: Create a separate VPC per department
explanation: After resources are tagged and the tags are activated as cost allocation tags, Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report can group costs by those tags. VPCs and IAM groups organize networking and permissions, not billing data.

question: A company wants to be notified automatically when its spending pattern suddenly deviates from normal, using machine learning to detect the change. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to spot unusual spending and sends alerts with root-cause details. A CloudWatch billing alarm fires only when charges cross a fixed threshold, and Compute Optimizer gives right-sizing advice.

question: A company needs a 30-minute response time for business-critical outages and access to a pool of Technical Account Managers, at the lowest cost. Which Support plan should it choose?
explanation: Enterprise On-Ramp gives a 30-minute response for business-critical issues and a pool of TAMs. Enterprise Support adds a 15-minute response and a designated TAM but costs more than the requirement needs.

question: A startup needs 24/7 phone and chat access to cloud support engineers and the full set of Trusted Advisor checks for the lowest price. Which Support plan meets these needs?
explanation: Business Support is the lowest-cost plan with 24/7 phone and chat, full Trusted Advisor checks and a 1-hour production-down response. Developer Support offers only business-hours email and the core Trusted Advisor checks.

question: Which AWS Enterprise Support feature gives customers a team of billing and account experts for non-technical billing questions?
explanation: The Concierge Support Team, included in Enterprise Support, handles billing and account questions. The Technical Account Manager is the customer's technical advocate for architecture and operations, not billing.

question: A developer on the Basic Support plan wants free, community-driven answers to a technical question from AWS experts and other users. Which resource should the developer use?
explanation: AWS re:Post is a free community Q&A site where AWS experts and users answer questions. Prescriptive Guidance publishes strategies and patterns, but it is not a place to ask questions.

question: A company wants to buy a third-party firewall appliance, deploy it in minutes and pay for it through its AWS bill. Which resource should it use?
explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated catalog of third-party software that can be deployed quickly and billed through the AWS account. The Partner Network is a program for consulting and technology partners, not a software storefront.

question: A company notices that an Amazon EC2 instance in another AWS account is sending spam and port scans to its servers. Whom should the company report this to?
explanation: The AWS Abuse team (AWS Trust & Safety) investigates reports of AWS resources used for spam, port scanning, DDoS or other abuse. AWS Health Dashboard shows service events affecting your own account and does not take abuse reports.

question: A company wants to stop guessing how many servers it will need for a product launch next quarter. Which advantage of cloud computing does this describe?
optionC: Benefit from massive economies of scale
optionD: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explanation: In the cloud a company provisions what it needs and scales up or down with demand, so it no longer has to forecast capacity in advance. Economies of scale lower prices, but they do not remove the need to forecast server counts.

question: A company wants to replace large upfront hardware purchases with monthly payments based only on what it actually uses. Which advantage of cloud computing applies?
optionC: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
optionD: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explanation: Paying only for consumed resources turns capital expenditure on hardware into variable operating expense. Stopping spending on data centers is a related advantage, but it describes freeing staff from facility work, not the CapEx-to-OpEx pricing shift.

question: Why is AWS able to offer lower pay-as-you-go prices than most companies could achieve by running their own data centers?
optionA: Aggregated usage from many customers creates economies of scale
optionB: Each customer receives dedicated physical hardware
optionC: Customers pay for reserved capacity instead of usage
optionD: Customers are responsible for maintaining the physical data center facilities
explanation: Because AWS aggregates usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, it achieves higher economies of scale and passes the savings on as lower prices. Customers never maintain AWS facilities; physical security and maintenance are AWS's responsibility.

question: A company wants its developers to experiment with new ideas by launching test environments in minutes and discarding them cheaply. Which cloud benefit does this represent?
explanation: Agility means resources are available in minutes, so the cost and time of experimenting drops sharply. High availability is about keeping workloads running during failures, not about how fast teams can try new ideas.

question: A company wants its ticketing website to add servers automatically during sudden demand spikes and remove them when demand drops. Which cloud concept is this?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to acquire resources as demand rises and release them as it falls, typically with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling. Fault tolerance keeps a system running when components fail, which is a different goal.

question: A company wants to serve customers in Asia and Europe with low latency within days, without building any new data centers. Which cloud advantage is this?
optionC: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
optionD: Benefit from massive economies of scale
explanation: AWS Regions around the world let a company deploy close to customers in a few clicks. Stop guessing capacity is about sizing infrastructure, not about geographic reach.

question: A company wants its web application to keep running if a single data center in its AWS Region fails. What should the company do?
optionA: Use a larger EC2 instance type
optionB: Deploy the application across multiple Availability Zones
optionC: Purchase Reserved Instances for the servers
optionD: Add more EC2 instances inside the same single Availability Zone
explanation: Each Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with independent power and networking, so spreading instances across AZs survives a data center failure. Adding instances in the same AZ still leaves a single point of failure.

question: Which term describes a system's ability to handle a growing workload by adding resources, such as more instances or storage?
explanation: Scalability is the ability to grow to meet increased load, either by adding instances or by using larger ones. Durability refers to protecting stored data from loss, not to handling more workload.

question: A company wants its IT staff to build customer features instead of racking servers and managing power and cooling. Which cloud advantage applies?
optionA: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explanation: AWS handles the heavy lifting of racking, stacking, and powering servers, so staff can focus on customers. Speed and agility is related but describes how quickly resources can be provisioned, not removing facility work.

question: A company moving to AWS wants to know which security benefit it gains automatically for the physical infrastructure. Which statement is correct?
optionA: AWS patches the guest operating systems on all EC2 instances
optionB: AWS configures the customer's security group rules
optionC: AWS manages permissions for the customer's IAM users
optionD: AWS secures the data centers, hardware, and global network
explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for security of the cloud: facilities, hardware, and network infrastructure. Patching the guest operating system on EC2 remains the customer's job.

question: A company runs a reporting workload only during the last three days of each month. Which cloud benefit lowers its cost most directly?
optionA: Pay-as-you-go pricing for resources actually used
optionB: Global reach through hundreds of CloudFront edge locations
optionC: Eleven nines of durability in Amazon S3
explanation: With pay-as-you-go pricing the company pays only while the reporting resources run and can shut them down for the rest of the month. Multi-AZ deployment improves availability but adds cost rather than removing it.

question: A company wants its e-commerce site to remain operational even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. Which approach meets this requirement?
optionA: Deploy across multiple Availability Zones in one Region
optionB: Deploy the workload in more than one AWS Region
optionC: Use larger EC2 instances in the current Region
optionD: Keep backups in the same Availability Zone
explanation: Only a multi-Region deployment protects against the loss of a whole Region. Multiple Availability Zones protect against a data center failure, but all of them sit inside the single affected Region.

question: A company wants to run and monitor systems, make frequent small reversible changes, and learn from operational failures. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?
explanation: Operational excellence covers running and monitoring systems, performing operations as code, and making frequent, small, reversible changes. Reliability focuses on recovering from failures and meeting demand, not on improving operational procedures.

question: Which Well-Architected pillar includes the design principles of implementing a strong identity foundation and enabling traceability?
explanation: A strong identity foundation, traceability, and applying security at all layers are design principles of the security pillar. Operational excellence includes observability, but identity and traceability for protection belong to security.

question: A company wants its workload to recover automatically from infrastructure failures and to perform its intended function consistently. Which pillar addresses this?
explanation: The reliability pillar covers automatically recovering from failure, testing recovery procedures, and scaling horizontally. Performance efficiency is about using resources efficiently, not about recovering from failures.

question: A company wants to select the most suitable resource types, adopt serverless architectures, and experiment more often as requirements change. Which pillar applies?
explanation: Performance efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently, including serverless architectures, democratizing advanced technologies, and experimenting more often. Cost optimization also involves choosing resources, but its goal is the lowest price rather than meeting performance requirements.

question: A company wants to stop paying for idle resources, adopt a consumption model, and attribute spending to teams. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?
explanation: Cost optimization principles include adopting a consumption model, measuring overall efficiency, and analyzing and attributing expenditure. Sustainability also reduces waste, but its goal is environmental impact rather than spending.

question: A company wants to minimize the environmental impact of its workloads by maximizing utilization and reducing energy consumption. Which pillar addresses this?
explanation: The sustainability pillar, added in 2021, focuses on reducing environmental impact through higher utilization and more efficient hardware and software. Cost optimization often lowers usage too, but it targets spending rather than energy and emissions.

question: A company wants its architecture to assume that any component can fail at any time and to keep the application running anyway. Which design principle is this?
explanation: Designing for failure means building redundancy and automatic recovery so that no single component failure stops the application. Tightly coupled components do the opposite, because one failure cascades to the others.

question: A company wants its order service to keep accepting orders even when the downstream fulfillment service is temporarily unavailable. Which approach supports this?
optionA: Run both services on one large EC2 instance
optionB: Connect the services with synchronous API calls
optionC: Decouple the services with an Amazon SQS queue
optionD: Place both services in the same Availability Zone
explanation: An SQS queue buffers orders so the producer keeps working while the consumer is down, and the consumer processes the backlog when it recovers. Synchronous API calls create tight coupling, so a failed fulfillment service would block order intake.

question: Which statement best describes loose coupling in a cloud architecture?
optionA: Components share one database server and memory space
optionB: Components must always be updated, tested, and deployed together at once
optionC: Each component runs on dedicated physical hardware
optionD: Components interact through interfaces and can fail independently
explanation: Loosely coupled components communicate through well-defined interfaces such as queues or APIs, so a change or failure in one does not break the others. Having to deploy everything together is a sign of tight coupling.

question: A company wants to handle increasing web traffic by adding more EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer. What type of scaling is this?
explanation: Adding more instances is horizontal scaling (scaling out), which also removes single points of failure. Vertical scaling means moving to a larger instance, which has size limits and keeps one point of failure.

question: A company wants to create identical, repeatable environments from templates instead of configuring resources manually in the console. Which AWS service supports this?
explanation: CloudFormation provisions resources from infrastructure-as-code templates, supporting the design principle of performing operations as code. AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations, but it does not build environments.

question: A company wants to reduce time spent on database patching, backups, and hardware provisioning. Which approach best follows AWS design principles?
optionA: Install the database software on Amazon EC2 instances
optionB: Keep the database on on-premises servers
optionC: Use a managed database service such as Amazon RDS
optionD: Attach larger EBS volumes to the database server
explanation: Managed services such as Amazon RDS handle patching, backups, and hardware so teams can focus on applications. Running the database on EC2 leaves operating system and database maintenance with the customer.

question: A company wants any web server to be replaceable at any time without losing user session data. Which design practice supports this?
optionA: Keep session data on the local disk of each instance
optionB: Store session state externally in Amazon DynamoDB
optionC: Assign an Elastic IP address to every server
optionD: Increase the size of each web server
explanation: Keeping servers stateless, with session data in a shared store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache, lets any instance be terminated or replaced. Data on a local disk is lost when the instance is replaced.

question: A company wants to protect its application with controls at the edge, the VPC, the subnet, the instance, and the code. Which security design principle is this?
explanation: Applying security at all layers means defense in depth across edge, network, compute, and application controls. Enabling traceability is also a security principle, but it concerns logging and monitoring actions rather than layered defenses.

question: A company wants to address skills gaps, new job roles, and organizational change management as it moves to the cloud. Which AWS CAF perspective covers this?
explanation: The People perspective bridges technology and business through culture, workforce transformation, and change management. Governance focuses on program and risk management rather than skills and roles.

question: A company wants to manage cloud program risk, track cloud spending, and maximize the benefits of its cloud investments. Which AWS CAF perspective covers this?
explanation: The Governance perspective orchestrates cloud initiatives through program and project management, risk management, and cloud financial management. Operations focuses on running services day to day, not on financial and risk oversight.

question: A company wants to move hundreds of on-premises virtual machines to Amazon EC2 quickly without changing the applications. Which migration strategy should it use?
explanation: Rehosting, or lift and shift, moves applications as they are and is the fastest way to migrate at scale. Refactoring re-architects the application, which takes far more time and effort.

question: A company wants to move its self-managed MySQL database to Amazon RDS during migration without changing application code. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Replatforming (lift, tinker, and shift) makes a few cloud optimizations, such as moving to a managed database, without changing the core architecture. Rehosting would move the database server as it is onto EC2.

question: A company wants to replace its on-premises customer relationship management application with a software as a service (SaaS) product. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Repurchasing means moving to a different product, commonly a SaaS offering, and dropping the existing application. Replatforming keeps the same application while making small optimizations.

question: A company wants to re-architect a monolithic application into serverless microservices to add features and improve scalability. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Refactoring (re-architecting) changes how the application is built to use cloud-native features, driven by needs that are hard to meet in the current design. Replatforming makes only minor optimizations without changing the architecture.

question: A company wants one central place to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner tools. Which AWS service should it use?
explanation: AWS Migration Hub provides a single location to discover, plan, and track migrations across AWS and partner solutions. Application Migration Service performs rehost replication, but it is one of the tools Migration Hub tracks, not the tracking dashboard.

question: A company wants to gather server specifications, utilization data, and dependencies from its on-premises data center to plan a migration. Which AWS service helps?
explanation: Application Discovery Service collects configuration, usage, and dependency data from on-premises servers to help plan migrations. Application Migration Service performs the actual lift-and-shift replication after planning.

question: A company wants to lift and shift physical and virtual servers to AWS with continuous block-level replication and minimal cutover downtime. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) continuously replicates source servers to AWS and launches them with short cutover windows, making it the recommended rehost tool. Application Discovery Service only collects planning data and does not move servers.

question: A company wants to migrate an Oracle database to Amazon Aurora while keeping the source database fully operational during the migration. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS DMS migrates databases while the source stays operational and supports heterogeneous migrations, with the Schema Conversion Tool converting the schema. DataSync copies files and objects, not live database changes.

question: A company wants to move 500 TB of archived data to AWS, but its internet connection would take months to transfer it. Which service should it use?
explanation: Snowball Edge devices move large datasets physically, which is faster than a slow network for hundreds of terabytes. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over the internet but still depends on the limited connection.

question: A company wants to automate recurring online transfers of files from on-premises NFS shares to Amazon S3 and Amazon EFS. Which service should it use?
explanation: DataSync automates and accelerates online data movement between on-premises storage such as NFS or SMB shares and AWS storage services. Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, and FTP endpoints for partners, not scheduled bulk copies from file shares.

question: A company is comparing on-premises costs with AWS. Which of these is a fixed, upfront expense in a traditional data center?
optionA: Paying per second for EC2 instance usage
optionB: Paying per gigabyte of Amazon S3 storage used
optionC: Buying physical servers and storage arrays
optionD: Paying per request for AWS Lambda functions
explanation: Hardware purchases are capital expenditures paid upfront regardless of later usage, which makes them a fixed cost. EC2, S3, and Lambda charges are variable costs that track actual consumption.

question: A company finds that its Amazon EC2 instances average 5 percent CPU utilization all month. Which cost optimization action should it take first?
optionA: Add more instances to the Auto Scaling group
optionB: Move the instances to Dedicated Hosts
optionC: Migrate the same instances to a different AWS Region for lower prices
optionD: Right-size the instances to smaller instance types
explanation: Right-sizing matches instance types to actual workload needs, and AWS Compute Optimizer recommends smaller sizes for underused instances. Adding instances would increase spending on capacity that is already idle.

question: A company wants to use its existing Microsoft Windows Server and SQL Server licenses on AWS to reduce costs. Which licensing approach supports this?
explanation: BYOL lets a company apply licenses it already owns, often on Dedicated Hosts, and AWS License Manager helps track them. License-included instances bundle the license cost into the hourly price, so the company would pay for licenses twice.

question: A company wants to cut costs by automatically stopping its development EC2 instances every night and weekend. Which approach should it use?
optionA: Purchase three-year Reserved Instances for development
optionB: Move the development instances to Dedicated Hosts
optionC: Increase the instance sizes to finish work faster
optionD: Automate stop and start schedules for the instances
explanation: Automation such as Instance Scheduler on AWS or Systems Manager stops instances when no one needs them, so the company pays nothing for compute while they are off. Reserved Instances bill for the full term whether or not the instances run, which suits steady workloads rather than part-time ones.

question: When estimating total cost of ownership, which cost does a company typically reduce by moving a self-managed database to Amazon RDS?
optionA: Data transfer charges for traffic out to the internet
optionB: Per-gigabyte charges for stored database data
optionC: Staff time for patching, backups, and maintenance
optionD: Monthly fees for an AWS Support plan
explanation: Managed services take over undifferentiated operational tasks, lowering labor costs that are a large part of TCO. Data transfer out is still charged whether the database is self-managed or on RDS.

question: Which on-premises data center cost is often overlooked when a company compares its current spending with AWS pricing?
optionA: Per-request charges for Amazon API Gateway calls
optionD: Power, cooling, and physical facility space
explanation: Facility costs such as power, cooling, real estate, and physical security are indirect costs that belong in a TCO comparison. Data transfer between Availability Zones is an AWS charge, not an on-premises cost.

question: A company wants to compare the full cost of running workloads on premises against AWS, including hardware, facilities, and staff. Which concept should it evaluate?
explanation: TCO captures both direct and indirect costs, including hardware, facilities, power, and labor, over the life of the workload. RPO and RTO are disaster recovery targets, not cost measures.

question: A company wants the lowest compute cost for fault-tolerant batch jobs that can be stopped and restarted at any time. Which pricing model fits best?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90 percent off On-Demand prices but can be interrupted with a two-minute warning, which batch jobs can tolerate. Reserved Instances require a one- or three-year commitment and suit steady workloads instead.

question: A company has a steady workload that must run without interruption for the next three years. Which pricing model offers the greatest savings?
explanation: Reserved Instances with a three-year term provide up to 72 percent off On-Demand prices for steady, predictable usage. Spot Instances can be cheaper but may be interrupted, which this workload cannot tolerate.

question: A company is launching a short-term project with unpredictable usage that cannot be interrupted and does not allow any long-term commitment. Which pricing model fits?
explanation: On-Demand Instances need no commitment and run until the company stops them, which suits short, unpredictable workloads. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances require one- or three-year commitments, and Spot Instances can be interrupted.

question: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task is the company's responsibility?
optionA: Maintaining the physical hosts in the data center
optionC: Patching the hypervisor that runs the instances
optionD: Replacing failed storage hardware in the Region
explanation: EC2 is infrastructure as a service, so the customer patches and secures the guest operating system and everything above it. The hypervisor, host hardware and facilities are security of the cloud, which AWS owns.

question: A company moves its relational database to Amazon RDS. Which task remains the company's responsibility under the shared responsibility model?
optionB: Managing database user accounts and permissions
optionD: Applying operating system patches to the database host
explanation: On RDS, AWS patches the database engine and host operating system and maintains the hardware. The customer still controls who can access the database, including database users, IAM access and network rules.

question: Which statement best summarizes the AWS shared responsibility model?
optionA: AWS secures all customer data once any support plan is purchased
optionB: Customers secure hardware; AWS secures customer data
optionC: AWS and customers split every security control equally
optionD: AWS secures the cloud; customers secure what they put in it
explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (infrastructure, hardware, facilities), while customers are responsible for security IN the cloud (data, identities, configuration). No support plan transfers data protection to AWS.

question: A developer deploys application code to AWS Lambda. Which responsibility remains with the developer rather than with AWS?
optionA: Patching the operating system that runs functions
optionB: Scaling the physical compute fleet behind Lambda
optionC: Maintaining the runtime hosts in each Availability Zone
optionD: Securing the function code and its IAM permissions
explanation: With Lambda, AWS manages the servers, operating system, runtime patching and scaling. The customer remains responsible for its own code, the data it handles and the IAM permissions granted to the function.

question: A company stores confidential documents in Amazon S3. Which security task is the company responsible for?
optionA: Replicating objects across multiple devices for durability
optionB: Securing storage hardware inside AWS facilities
optionC: Configuring bucket policies and Block Public Access
optionD: Destroying disks that once held customer data
explanation: Access control on buckets and objects is security in the cloud, so the customer configures bucket policies and Block Public Access. Durability, storage hardware and media destruction are handled by AWS.

question: Which of the following is an example of a shared control between AWS and the customer?
explanation: Patch management is shared: AWS patches the infrastructure, and customers patch their guest operating systems and applications. Physical security is AWS only, and data classification is the customer's alone.

question: Awareness and training is listed as a shared control in the AWS shared responsibility model. What does this mean?
optionA: AWS trains every customer employee on security at no charge
optionB: AWS trains its employees; customers train their own employees
optionC: Customers must train AWS data center staff
optionD: Only AWS Partners may deliver security training
explanation: For shared controls, each party applies the control within its own scope: AWS trains AWS staff and customers train their own people. AWS does not take over customer staff training.

question: A company runs containers on Amazon ECS and is deciding between EC2 instances and AWS Fargate. How does choosing Fargate change its responsibilities?
optionA: The company must now patch the host kernel
optionB: AWS becomes responsible for container image code
optionC: The company no longer needs IAM permissions
optionD: AWS manages and patches the underlying servers
explanation: Fargate is serverless compute for containers, so AWS provisions, patches and scales the underlying hosts. The customer still owns its container images, application code and IAM configuration.

question: A company's security officer asks who protects the data center buildings that host the company's Amazon EC2 instances. What is the correct answer?
optionD: The AWS Partner that resells the account
explanation: Physical and environmental security of AWS facilities is entirely AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model. Customers never manage data center access, whatever service they use.

question: A company stores application data in Amazon DynamoDB tables. Which task is the company's responsibility?
optionB: Controlling IAM access to its tables
optionD: Expanding the physical network capacity of the Region
explanation: DynamoDB is fully managed, so AWS handles servers, patching and storage hardware. The customer decides who can read and write its tables through IAM and protects the data it stores.

question: A company stores sensitive data on Amazon EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances. Who is responsible for enabling encryption of that data at rest?
optionB: AWS Support, once a support plan exists
optionD: The AWS compliance team through AWS Artifact
explanation: Protecting customer data, including choosing to encrypt EBS volumes with KMS keys, is the customer's responsibility. AWS provides the encryption feature, but the customer must enable and manage it.

question: Which responsibility belongs to AWS for every AWS service, regardless of whether it is infrastructure, container or managed?
optionA: Configuring the security group rules for customer instances
optionC: Protecting the infrastructure that runs the services
explanation: AWS always protects the global infrastructure: hardware, software, networking and facilities that run AWS services. Security groups, IAM credentials and data encryption choices remain customer tasks.

question: A company replaces self-managed MySQL on Amazon EC2 with Amazon RDS for MySQL. Which responsibility moves from the company to AWS?
optionA: Controlling which users can query the data
optionB: Installing database engine and OS patches
optionC: Encrypting sensitive columns in the application
optionD: Restricting network access to the database port
explanation: Moving to RDS hands database engine and operating system patching to AWS. User access, application-level encryption and security group rules stay with the customer.

question: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2. Who is responsible for configuring the security group rules that control inbound traffic to the instances?
optionD: AWS Managed Services, for every account
explanation: Network and firewall configuration, including security group rules, is security in the cloud and belongs to the customer. AWS provides the feature but does not decide which traffic a workload should allow.

question: A company must make sure data sent from users' browsers to its application on AWS is encrypted. Who is responsible for configuring that encryption in transit?
optionA: AWS, which encrypts all traffic automatically
optionB: AWS Shield, which encrypts web requests
optionC: The customer, for example by enforcing TLS
optionD: The edge location operators in each Region
explanation: Network traffic protection for a customer's application is the customer's responsibility, typically by using HTTPS with TLS certificates. AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks and does not encrypt traffic.

question: A startup wants to minimize the infrastructure it must secure, patch and manage. Which compute option shifts the most responsibility to AWS?
explanation: With Lambda, AWS manages servers, operating systems, runtimes and scaling, leaving the customer mainly its code and permissions. EC2 instances, Dedicated Hosts and Outposts all leave the guest operating system to the customer.

question: A company's external auditors request a copy of the AWS SOC 2 report. Which AWS service should the company use to download it?
explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS compliance reports such as SOC, PCI and ISO, plus agreements like the BAA. Audit Manager collects evidence about the customer's own usage, not AWS's reports.

question: A company wants to continuously and automatically collect evidence from its own AWS usage to prepare for a PCI DSS audit. Which service should it use?
explanation: Audit Manager maps a customer's AWS usage to frameworks like PCI DSS and gathers audit-ready evidence automatically. Artifact only provides AWS's own compliance reports and agreements.

question: A security team must find out which IAM user deleted an Amazon S3 bucket last week. Which AWS service records this information?
explanation: CloudTrail records API calls, including who made the call, from where and when, so it answers who deleted the bucket. CloudWatch tracks metrics and logs for performance, not an audit of API activity.

question: A company needs to track configuration changes to its resources over time and flag security groups that allow unrestricted SSH access. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Config records resource configuration history and evaluates it against rules, such as restricted SSH, to report compliance. CloudTrail logs the API calls but does not evaluate resource configurations against rules.

question: An operations team wants to be notified when an EC2 instance's CPU utilization stays above 80 percent for ten minutes. Which service should it use?
explanation: CloudWatch collects metrics such as CPU utilization and triggers alarms with notifications when thresholds are breached. CloudTrail audits API calls and does not monitor performance metrics.

question: A company wants a managed service to create and control encryption keys that integrates natively with Amazon S3 and Amazon EBS. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS KMS creates and manages encryption keys, integrates with S3, EBS and most other services, and logs key use in CloudTrail. CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware but requires more management and is chosen for single-tenant requirements.

question: Regulations require a company to store its encryption keys in dedicated single-tenant hardware security modules that it exclusively controls. Which service meets this requirement?
optionA: AWS KMS with AWS managed keys
explanation: CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant FIPS-validated hardware security modules under the customer's exclusive control. AWS KMS uses HSMs too, but they are multi-tenant and managed by AWS.

question: An application has database passwords hard-coded in its source files. The company wants to store them centrally and rotate them automatically. Which service should it use?
explanation: Secrets Manager stores credentials securely, lets applications retrieve them at runtime and rotates them automatically. KMS manages encryption keys, not application secrets with rotation.

question: A company needs public SSL/TLS certificates for its Application Load Balancer that are provisioned at no extra cost and renewed automatically. Which service should it use?
explanation: ACM issues public TLS certificates for integrated services such as ELB and CloudFront at no additional cost and renews them automatically. KMS manages encryption keys, not certificates.

question: Data residency laws require a company to keep customer data inside the European Union. How can the company control where its data is stored on AWS?
optionA: Deploy resources only in EU Regions
optionB: Enable AWS Shield Advanced on all accounts
optionC: Ask AWS Support to place the data
optionD: Store data in EU edge locations
explanation: Customers choose the Region where content is stored, and AWS does not move it out of that Region without customer action. Edge locations cache content for delivery and are not a data residency control.

question: Which scenario is an example of protecting data with encryption in transit?
optionA: Enabling default encryption on an S3 bucket
optionB: Encrypting an EBS volume with a KMS key
explanation: Encryption in transit protects data moving across a network, as TLS does for HTTPS. Encrypting S3 objects, EBS volumes and RDS snapshots protects data at rest.

question: A company wants to automatically discover sensitive data, such as credit card numbers and personal information, stored in its Amazon S3 buckets. Which service should it use?
explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to find and report sensitive data such as PII in S3. GuardDuty detects threats from log analysis but does not classify data content.

question: A company wants intelligent threat detection that analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to find activity such as cryptocurrency mining. Which service fits?
explanation: GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to detect malicious or unauthorized behavior. Detective helps investigate findings after they occur rather than detecting threats itself.

question: A company wants automated, continual scanning of its EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities. Which service should it use?
explanation: Inspector scans EC2, ECR container images and Lambda functions for known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and unintended network exposure. GuardDuty detects active threats from logs, not software vulnerabilities.

question: A security team wants one place that aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie and checks accounts against security best practice standards. Which service fits?
explanation: Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes findings from AWS security services and runs automated checks against standards such as the CIS benchmarks. Detective is for investigating root causes, not aggregating posture.

question: After GuardDuty reports a suspicious finding, an analyst must investigate its root cause by visualizing related activity over time. Which service should the analyst use?
explanation: Detective builds a linked graph from logs so analysts can investigate the root cause and scope of findings. Security Hub aggregates findings but does not provide that investigation graph.

question: A company plans to run a penetration test against its own EC2 instances. What does the AWS penetration testing policy require?
optionA: No prior approval for permitted services
optionB: Written approval from AWS Support first
optionC: A subscription to AWS Shield Advanced
optionD: A request submitted through AWS Artifact
explanation: AWS allows customers to run penetration tests against a list of permitted services, including EC2, without prior approval. Prohibited activities such as DoS flooding are still not allowed.

question: A company's public website suffers frequent DDoS attacks and needs 24/7 access to the Shield Response Team plus protection from scaling charges. Which service should it use?
explanation: Shield Advanced adds enhanced DDoS detection, 24/7 Shield Response Team access and cost protection for attack-related scaling. Shield Standard is free and automatic but includes neither the response team nor cost protection.

question: A company needs to block SQL injection and cross-site scripting requests before they reach its web application behind Amazon CloudFront. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that filters HTTP requests with rules for attacks such as SQL injection and XSS. Shield Standard defends against network-layer DDoS attacks, not application-layer exploits.

question: A company needs a managed, stateful network firewall with intrusion prevention to filter traffic at the perimeter of its entire VPC. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a managed service providing stateful inspection and intrusion prevention for VPC traffic. AWS WAF only inspects web (HTTP/HTTPS) requests to specific resources.

question: A company with many accounts in AWS Organizations wants to centrally configure and enforce AWS WAF rules and security group policies across all accounts. Which service fits?
explanation: Firewall Manager centrally manages WAF rules, Shield Advanced, security group policies and Network Firewall across accounts in an organization. Network Firewall is the firewall itself, not the cross-account policy manager.

question: A company wants to guarantee that no user can accidentally make objects in its Amazon S3 buckets publicly readable. Which feature should it enable?
optionB: S3 Block Public Access at the account level
explanation: S3 Block Public Access overrides any bucket policy or ACL that would grant public access, and setting it at the account level covers every bucket. Versioning and MFA Delete protect against deletion, Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, and Macie finds sensitive data but does not block access.

question: A company must block a specific malicious IP address range from reaching every instance in a subnet. Which VPC feature should it use?
explanation: Network ACLs apply at the subnet level and support explicit deny rules, so they can block an IP range. Security groups support only allow rules, so they cannot explicitly deny an address.

question: A company wants free automated checks that flag security groups with unrestricted ports and confirm that MFA is enabled on the root user. Which service provides these?
explanation: Trusted Advisor core security checks, free for all accounts, include unrestricted security group ports and root user MFA. Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities rather than account configuration best practices.

question: An administrator must give twelve developers identical permissions and be able to change them all at once later. What is the most efficient approach?
optionA: Attach the same inline policy to each user
optionB: Share one IAM user's credentials among them
optionC: Add the users to an IAM group with a policy
optionD: Give each developer the root user password
explanation: Attaching a policy to an IAM group grants it to every member, and one change updates them all. Separate inline policies must be edited user by user, and shared credentials break accountability.

question: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to read objects from an S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant this access?
optionA: Store an IAM user's access keys on the instance
optionB: Embed root user access keys in the code
optionD: Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
explanation: An IAM role attached through an instance profile supplies temporary, automatically rotated credentials to the application. Storing long-term access keys on the instance risks leaking them.

question: Which statement describes the principle of least privilege?
optionA: Grant administrator access, then trim it during audits
optionB: Give every user read-only access to all services
optionC: Grant only the permissions required for a task
optionD: Grant permissions based on each user's seniority
explanation: Least privilege means granting only the permissions needed to perform a task, and nothing more. Starting broad and trimming later leaves excess access in place in the meantime.

question: A company has just created a new AWS account. Which actions should it take to protect the root user?
optionA: Create root access keys for daily automation
optionB: Enable MFA and avoid using it for daily tasks
optionC: Share the root password with the operations team
optionD: Delete the root user after creating IAM users
explanation: Best practice is to enable MFA on the root user, avoid root access keys and use the root user only for tasks that require it. The root user cannot simply be deleted from a standalone account, and sharing it removes accountability.

question: In a standalone AWS account, which task requires signing in as the root user?
explanation: Closing a standalone account is one of the few tasks that require root user credentials. Creating groups, launching instances and viewing CloudTrail history can be granted to IAM identities.

question: An employee uses the AWS CLI on a workstation to call AWS APIs with long-term IAM user credentials. Which credential type does the CLI require?
optionA: A console user name and password
optionC: An access key ID and secret access key
explanation: Programmatic access through the CLI, SDKs or APIs uses an access key ID and secret access key. A console password only signs in to the AWS Management Console, and EC2 key pairs are for logging in to instances.

question: A company with 40 AWS accounts wants employees to sign in once with their corporate directory credentials and reach their assigned accounts. Which service should it use?
explanation: IAM Identity Center provides single sign-on for workforce users across all accounts in an organization and connects to existing identity providers. Cognito is designed for customers of applications, not employees.

question: A mobile app needs sign-up and sign-in for millions of customers, including sign-in through social identity providers. Which AWS service should the developers use?
explanation: Cognito provides user sign-up, sign-in and federation with social providers for web and mobile app users at scale. IAM Identity Center manages workforce access to AWS accounts, not app customers.

question: An auditing firm needs temporary access to resources in a company's AWS account without the company creating IAM users for it. What should the company configure?
optionA: An IAM user with shared access keys
optionB: The root user credentials protected by MFA
optionC: A security group allowing the firm's IP
optionD: A cross-account IAM role the firm can assume
explanation: A cross-account role lets identities in another account assume it and receive temporary credentials. Shared access keys are long-term, hard to audit and against best practice.

question: Which AWS service issues the temporary security credentials provided when an IAM role is assumed?
explanation: AWS STS issues short-lived credentials when a role is assumed or a federated user signs in. Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets but does not issue role credentials.

question: A company's AWS Lambda function must write logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs and read from DynamoDB. How should the company grant these permissions?
optionA: An execution role the function assumes
optionB: An IAM user with access keys for the function
optionC: A resource tag on the log group
optionD: A network ACL allowing the function
explanation: AWS services act on a customer's behalf through service roles, and Lambda uses an execution role for its permissions. Long-term IAM user keys in a function are unnecessary and riskier.

question: A security team requires every IAM user password to be at least 14 characters and include symbols. Which feature enforces this requirement?
explanation: The IAM account password policy sets length, complexity and rotation rules for IAM user passwords. An AWS Config rule can report whether such a policy exists, but it does not enforce password complexity.

question: A company using AWS Organizations must stop all member accounts, including their administrators, from using AWS Regions outside Europe. Which feature should it use?
explanation: SCPs set guardrails on the maximum permissions in member accounts, so they can deny actions in disallowed Regions even for administrators. Permission sets grant access to users but cannot restrict an account's administrators.

question: Which statement about service control policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations is correct?
optionA: They grant permissions to users in member accounts
optionB: They replace IAM policies in member accounts
optionC: They can be attached only to individual IAM users
optionD: They limit maximum permissions and grant none
explanation: SCPs define the maximum available permissions for accounts or OUs but never grant access themselves. IAM policies are still needed to grant permissions within those limits.

question: A company wants a second layer of protection for IAM user console sign-ins in case a password is stolen. What should it enable?
explanation: MFA requires a second factor, such as an authenticator app or security key, so a stolen password alone is not enough. A stronger password policy still relies on a single factor.

question: An auditor needs a list of all IAM users showing the status of their passwords, access keys and MFA devices. What should the administrator provide?
explanation: The IAM credential report lists every user and the status of their passwords, access keys and MFA devices. AWS Artifact holds AWS's compliance reports, not account credential details.

question: A security engineer wants to keep up with new AWS security features, best practices and solutions written by AWS security experts. Which resource should the engineer follow?
explanation: The AWS Security Blog publishes security announcements, best practices and solution walkthroughs by AWS experts. The AWS Health Dashboard reports service events affecting accounts, not guidance articles.

question: A developer has a question about securing an S3 bucket and wants answers from the AWS community and AWS experts in a Q&A forum. Which resource fits?
explanation: AWS re:Post is the community Q&A service where AWS experts and users answer questions, and it also hosts Knowledge Center articles. Trusted Advisor runs automated checks rather than answering questions.

question: A company wants to buy third-party firewall and endpoint protection software that runs on AWS and is billed through its AWS account. Where should it look?
explanation: AWS Marketplace is a catalog of third-party software, including security products, that can be deployed on AWS and billed on the AWS bill. Security Hub integrates partner findings but does not sell software.

question: A company lacks in-house security expertise and wants AWS experts to help design and implement its cloud security architecture. Which AWS option should it consider?
explanation: AWS Professional Services, like consulting partners in the AWS Partner Network, provides experts who help design and implement solutions. Trusted Advisor only gives automated recommendations, not hands-on help.

question: A developer wants to manage AWS resources by running repeatable commands and shell scripts from a laptop terminal. Which tool should the developer use?
explanation: The AWS CLI issues AWS API calls as terminal commands that can be scripted and repeated. The Management Console is a browser-based point-and-click interface, so it is not suited to scripting.

question: A company wants to provision identical development, test and production environments repeatedly from version-controlled JSON or YAML templates. Which AWS service meets this need?
explanation: CloudFormation is infrastructure as code: a template in JSON or YAML defines resources that are created the same way every time as a stack. AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations but does not provision them.

question: Developers on a team prefer to define cloud infrastructure in familiar programming languages such as TypeScript and Python instead of templates. Which AWS offering supports this?
explanation: The CDK lets developers model infrastructure as code in general-purpose languages and synthesizes it into CloudFormation templates. An AWS SDK calls service APIs from application code but is not an infrastructure-as-code framework.

question: A team wants to upload its Java web application code and let AWS automatically handle capacity provisioning, load balancing, scaling and health monitoring. Which service should the team use?
optionA: Amazon EC2 with manually configured instances
explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is a platform service: you upload code and it deploys and manages the underlying EC2, load balancing and Auto Scaling for you. CloudFormation can build the same resources but you must define and manage every one yourself.

question: Which statement best describes a hybrid cloud deployment model?
optionA: All workloads running entirely in AWS Regions
optionB: On-premises infrastructure connected to resources running in AWS
optionC: All workloads running in a private on-premises data center
optionD: Workloads spread across multiple Availability Zones in one Region
explanation: A hybrid deployment links existing on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources, often over VPN or Direct Connect. Running everything in AWS, even across several Availability Zones, is a cloud (cloud-native) deployment.

question: A financial firm needs a dedicated private network connection from its data center to AWS with consistent bandwidth that does not travel over the public internet. Which service should it use?
explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private link between a data center and AWS with more consistent performance than the internet. A Site-to-Site VPN is encrypted but still travels over the public internet.

question: A branch office needs an encrypted connection to its Amazon VPC that can be set up within hours using its existing internet link. Which option is most appropriate?
explanation: A Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec-encrypted tunnels over the existing internet connection and can be set up quickly at low cost. Direct Connect requires a physical circuit that typically takes weeks to provision.

question: A mobile app developer wants application code written in Java to read and write objects in Amazon S3 and items in DynamoDB directly. What should the developer use?
explanation: AWS SDKs provide language-specific libraries that let application code call AWS APIs programmatically. The CLI also calls the APIs, but from a terminal rather than from inside the application's own code.

question: An online retailer must keep its storefront running even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. Which approach meets this disaster recovery requirement?
optionA: Deploy across multiple Availability Zones in one Region
optionB: Move to larger EC2 instance types
optionC: Replicate the workload to a second AWS Region
optionD: Serve static content from more edge locations
explanation: Only a multi-Region design survives the loss of a whole Region, and a second Region can also bring the application closer to distant users. Multiple Availability Zones protect against a data center failure but all sit inside the same Region.

question: A company's web application must remain available if a single data center fails. Which architecture provides this high availability at the lowest complexity?
optionA: EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer
optionB: Larger EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone
optionC: One EC2 instance in a Local Zone
optionD: Content cached at multiple edge locations
explanation: Each Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with independent power and networking, so spreading instances across AZs behind a load balancer survives a data center failure. A bigger instance in one AZ is still a single point of failure.

question: A healthcare provider is legally required to keep patient records stored within its own country. What should it consider first when designing its AWS deployment?
optionA: Choosing an edge location inside that country
optionB: Enabling AWS Global Accelerator for the application
optionC: Spreading data across multiple Availability Zones
optionD: Choosing an AWS Region located in that country
explanation: Data stored in a Region stays in that Region unless the customer moves it, so Region choice is how data residency is met. Edge locations cache content for delivery and are not where a company chooses to store its primary data.

question: A media company wants to reduce latency for viewers around the world by caching its videos and images at sites close to them. Which AWS service should it use?
explanation: CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content at edge locations near viewers. Global Accelerator also uses the edge network but routes TCP and UDP traffic to endpoints without caching any content.

question: An online gaming company runs a UDP-based application and wants fixed static IP addresses that route players over the AWS global network to the healthiest regional endpoint. Which service fits best?
optionB: Network Load Balancer in one Region
explanation: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IP addresses and sends TCP or UDP traffic across the AWS backbone to the optimal healthy endpoint. CloudFront is designed for caching HTTP content, not for non-HTTP gaming traffic with static IPs.

question: A telecommunications partner wants to deploy applications for 5G mobile devices with ultra-low latency by running compute inside carrier networks. Which AWS offering is designed for this?
explanation: Wavelength Zones embed AWS compute and storage within telecom providers' 5G networks so traffic does not leave the carrier network. Local Zones place AWS infrastructure near large cities but not inside carrier 5G networks.

question: A manufacturer must run AWS services inside its own factory data center for low-latency access to local systems, using the same AWS APIs and tools. Which service should it choose?
explanation: Outposts delivers AWS-managed racks or servers into the customer's own facility, running AWS services with the same APIs. Local Zones are AWS-operated sites near population centers, not hardware installed on the customer's premises.

question: A film studio in a large city far from the nearest AWS Region needs single-digit millisecond latency for rendering workstations without installing hardware on site. Which option should it use?
explanation: Local Zones extend a Region with AWS-operated compute and storage close to large metropolitan areas for very low latency. Outposts would also give low latency, but it requires installing AWS hardware in the studio's own facility.

question: A company runs nightly image-processing jobs that can be stopped and restarted at any time without harm. Which EC2 purchasing option is most cost-effective?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off and suit interruption-tolerant workloads. On-Demand works but costs far more for jobs that can tolerate being interrupted.

question: A company must bring existing per-socket and per-core server software licenses to AWS and needs visibility into the physical server's sockets and cores. Which EC2 option meets this requirement?
explanation: A Dedicated Host is a whole physical server allocated to you, exposing sockets and cores for bring-your-own-license compliance. Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware but do not give visibility or control over the physical server.

question: An analytics application processes very large datasets entirely in RAM and needs a high ratio of memory to vCPU. Which EC2 instance family should be chosen?
explanation: Memory optimized instances are built for workloads that process large datasets in memory, such as in-memory databases and analytics. Compute optimized instances favor high CPU performance relative to memory.

question: Traffic to a news website spikes unpredictably during breaking stories. Which service automatically adds EC2 instances during spikes and removes them when demand drops?
explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling launches and terminates instances to match demand, which provides elasticity. CloudWatch supplies the metrics and alarms that can trigger scaling, but it does not launch instances by itself.

question: A company runs several microservices and needs to route HTTPS requests to different targets based on the URL path, such as /api or /images. Which load balancer type should it use?
explanation: An Application Load Balancer works at layer 7 and supports path-based and host-based routing for HTTP and HTTPS. A Network Load Balancer works at layer 4 and cannot inspect URL paths.

question: A photo-sharing app must create a thumbnail whenever a user uploads an image to Amazon S3, without the team managing any servers. Which service should run the thumbnail code?
explanation: Lambda runs code in response to events such as S3 uploads, scales automatically and bills only for execution time. EC2 could run the code but would require the team to provision and manage servers.

question: A company wants to run Docker containers on Amazon ECS without provisioning, patching or scaling the underlying EC2 instances. Which option should it use?
optionB: Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type
explanation: Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that removes the need to manage servers or clusters of instances. The ECS EC2 launch type still leaves the customer responsible for the EC2 instances in the cluster.

question: An organization already runs its containerized applications on Kubernetes on premises and wants AWS to manage the Kubernetes control plane in the cloud. Which service should it adopt?
explanation: EKS is a managed Kubernetes service that runs the control plane for you and is compatible with standard Kubernetes tooling. ECS is an AWS-native container orchestrator and does not run Kubernetes.

question: A small bakery with little cloud experience wants to launch a WordPress website on a simple virtual private server for a low, predictable monthly price. Which service is the best fit?
explanation: Lightsail bundles a virtual server, storage, and data transfer into simple fixed monthly plans with preconfigured apps such as WordPress. EC2 offers more flexibility but requires more setup and has less predictable pricing for beginners.

question: A research lab needs to run hundreds of thousands of computing jobs, with AWS queueing the jobs and provisioning the right amount of compute for each. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Batch manages job queues and dynamically provisions the optimal compute resources for large numbers of batch jobs. Lambda suits short event-driven functions and has a 15-minute maximum run time per invocation.

question: Which is a characteristic of serverless compute such as AWS Lambda compared with virtual machines on Amazon EC2?
optionA: No servers to manage, and you pay only for compute used
optionB: You choose, install and patch the guest operating system
optionC: You pay hourly for instances even when they sit idle
optionD: You must size and manage the cluster's worker nodes
explanation: With serverless compute AWS manages the servers and operating system, and billing is based on requests and execution time. Choosing and patching the operating system is a customer task on EC2 virtual machines, not on Lambda.

question: A company is migrating a legacy application that needs full administrative control of the operating system and custom kernel-level software. Which compute service should it use?
explanation: EC2 provides virtual machines where the customer has full control over the operating system and installed software. Lambda, Fargate, and App Runner abstract the operating system away, so custom kernel-level software cannot be installed.

question: A company runs MySQL on self-managed EC2 instances and wants AWS to handle patching, automated backups and Multi-AZ failover while keeping its relational schema. Which service should it move to?
optionD: MySQL on larger Amazon EC2 instances
explanation: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that automates patching, backups, and Multi-AZ failover. Staying on EC2 keeps the database self-hosted, so the company would still manage those tasks itself.

question: A gaming company needs a serverless NoSQL key-value database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale for player profiles. Which service should it choose?
explanation: DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless key-value and document database with consistent single-digit millisecond latency at any scale. RDS for PostgreSQL is relational and requires choosing and sizing database instances.

question: A social network wants to store users and the relationships between them to power friend-of-friend recommendations. Which database service is purpose-built for this?
explanation: Neptune is a managed graph database designed to store and query highly connected data such as social relationships. DocumentDB is a MongoDB-compatible document database and is not optimized for traversing relationships.

question: Business analysts need to run complex SQL queries across petabytes of historical sales data for reporting and business intelligence. Which AWS service should the company use?
explanation: Redshift is a columnar data warehouse built for analytical SQL queries over very large datasets. RDS is designed for transactional (OLTP) workloads and is not optimized for petabyte-scale analytics.

question: An application's relational database is overloaded by repeated identical read queries. The company wants to keep frequently accessed results in memory for microsecond responses. Which service should it add?
explanation: ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching with Redis OSS, Valkey, or Memcached, which offloads repeated reads from the database. CloudFront caches web content at edge locations, not database query results inside the application tier.

question: A company wants to migrate an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime, including converting the schema. Which AWS tools should it use?
optionA: AWS DataSync with AWS Snowball Edge
optionB: AWS DMS with the AWS Schema Conversion Tool
optionD: AWS Storage Gateway with AWS Backup
explanation: The Schema Conversion Tool converts the Oracle schema to PostgreSQL, and DMS replicates the data with continuous replication to minimize downtime. Application Migration Service rehosts whole servers and does not convert a database engine.

question: In an Amazon VPC, what makes a subnet a public subnet?
optionA: Its route table has a route to an internet gateway
optionB: Its network ACL allows all inbound HTTP traffic
optionC: Its instances use a security group that allows all ports
optionD: It sends outbound traffic through a NAT gateway
explanation: A subnet is public when its associated route table sends internet-bound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to an internet gateway. A subnet whose default route points to a NAT gateway is a private subnet, and permissive security groups or ACLs do not create a path to the internet.

question: Application servers in a private subnet must download operating system patches from the internet, but must not accept connections initiated from the internet. What should be added?
optionA: An internet gateway route from the private subnet
optionB: A NAT gateway in a public subnet
explanation: A NAT gateway lets instances in private subnets start outbound connections to the internet while blocking connections initiated from outside. Routing the private subnet straight to an internet gateway would make it public and expose the servers.

question: Which statement correctly compares security groups and network ACLs in an Amazon VPC?
optionA: Security groups are stateless; network ACLs are stateful
optionB: Both operate at the subnet level and support deny rules
optionC: Security groups are stateful; network ACLs are stateless
optionD: Network ACLs attach to instances; security groups attach to subnets
explanation: Security groups act at the instance (network interface) level, are stateful so return traffic is allowed automatically, and support only allow rules. Network ACLs act at the subnet level, are stateless, and support both allow and deny rules.

question: A company runs 40 VPCs across several accounts and also connects two on-premises data centers. It wants a central hub instead of managing a full mesh of peering connections. Which service fits?
explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks through a single gateway. VPC peering is one-to-one and not transitive, so 40 VPCs would need hundreds of separate peering connections.

question: A bank needs a private, dedicated network connection from its data center to AWS with consistent bandwidth that does not travel over the public internet. Which service should it use?
explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private link between on-premises networks and AWS with consistent performance. Site-to-Site VPN is encrypted and quick to set up, but it runs over the public internet, so its performance varies.

question: An application is deployed in three AWS Regions, and the company wants Amazon Route 53 to send each user to the Region that responds fastest for them. Which routing policy should it choose?
explanation: Latency-based routing answers DNS queries with the Region that has the lowest measured network latency for the user. Geolocation routing decides by the user's location, which is not always the fastest path.

question: A streaming media company wants to cache videos and images at edge locations worldwide so viewers get low-latency delivery. Which AWS service meets this need?
explanation: CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content at edge locations close to viewers. Global Accelerator also uses the AWS edge network, but it routes TCP and UDP traffic to endpoints and does not cache content.

question: Developers want to publish, secure and throttle REST APIs that invoke AWS Lambda functions, including API keys and usage plans for partners. Which service should they use?
explanation: API Gateway creates, publishes and secures REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs, with throttling, API keys and usage plans built in. AppSync is for managed GraphQL APIs, not REST APIs with usage plans.

question: A multiplayer game uses UDP servers in two Regions and needs two static anycast IP addresses that route players to the nearest healthy endpoint over the AWS network. Which service should be used?
explanation: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes TCP and UDP traffic over the AWS global network to the closest healthy endpoint. CloudFront caches HTTP content and does not provide static anycast IPs for UDP game traffic.

question: A company stores data in Amazon S3 with unpredictable, changing access patterns. It wants storage costs optimized automatically, with no retrieval fees and no lifecycle rules to maintain. Which storage class fits?
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers automatically based on usage, for a small monitoring fee and with no retrieval fees. Standard-IA charges per-GB retrieval fees, which can cost more when access is unpredictable.

question: Audit records must be kept for ten years, are almost never read, and a retrieval time of up to 48 hours is acceptable. Which S3 storage class has the lowest storage cost?
explanation: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class, built for long-term retention with retrievals within 12 to 48 hours. Glacier Flexible Retrieval restores data faster but costs more to store.

question: Log files in an S3 bucket should move to a cheaper storage class after 30 days and be deleted automatically after one year. Which S3 feature does this?
